To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) extant methods used to correct for cross section and time series dependence are not robust to the presence of both forms of dependence; (ii) the use of well-specified test statistics substantially alters inferences in common settings in the accounting literature.

(1) the extant methods used to correct for cross section dependence are not robust to time series dependence, (2) the extant method used to correct for time series dependence is not robust to cross section dependence, (3) the extant tests are not robust to the use a well specified test statistic in the presence of both forms of dependence, and (4) the use of a well specified test statistics alters inferences reported by prior research

the Z2 test and Newey West corrections are not robust to cross sectional and time serial dependence and that correcting for such dependence substantially changes inferences in the implied cost equity capital, cost of debt, and conservatism literatures.

the accounting research community should be more aware of the implications of cross sectional and time Series dependence, and should use methods that are more robust in settings in which both forms of dependence are present.

researchers must take into account the possibility of both forms of dependence when using cross sectional and time-series data.
